tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy COLD-SEASON single-column run, data/eqwefic/noahcold_scm, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-noahcold and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) kernels/noah_driver at ESM_DT = 0.01 s. THE ASSERTIONS BY CLAIM. CLAIM 1, the liquid budget: `dsh2o_dt_total` per layer against WRF's own (sh2o_out - sh2o_in)/dt, plus its new term checked in its own right by `melt` (against SNOPAC's EX) and `water_supply` (against SNOPAC's PRCP1). CLAIM 2, the total-water budget: `dsmc_dt_total` and `dsice_dt`, which say that the phase change moves water between liquid and ice within a layer and does not change the total -- an error leaking transport into the phase term passes claim 1 and fails this. CLAIM 3, the switches at zero tolerance: `phase_active`, the frozen sink's clamp decision made at the assembly's shared state against WRF's at its post-SMFLX state, and `melting`, SNOPAC's own branch. PRECONDITION, not a result: `supersaturation_active` = 0. BOTH NEW EDGES ARE LOAD-BEARING, CHECKED BY BREAKING THEM. Removing the snowmelt coupling library turns 5 of these 20 assertions red; setting `dew_to_soil` back to its snow-free default of 1 turns 3 red on the frost column. A coupling that passes with its edge cut proves nothing, so both were cut. THE REFERENCE STEP. Worst absolute residual over this document's assertions: 1.24e-11 at ESM_DT = 1e-6 s, 1.24e-15 at 0.01 s and 1.31e-18 at 60 s. Unlike every other document in this family this column's V HAS NO RIGHT-HAND BRANCH -- its clamp decisions are the same at all three passes, so the residual just keeps falling as the differenced reference gains digits, and 60 s is numerically the best of the three. That is worth recording precisely because it is the exception: the right branch of the V is a discrete clamp flip, not a smooth truncation error, so it is absent entirely until a column happens to sit near a threshold. 0.01 s is used anyway, for consistency with the other four documents and because the melt column shows what the 60 s pass can do. The bound is 1e-14, eight times the measured residual and above the eps(sh2o)/dt = 6.7e-15 floor it sits at. A NOTE ON WHAT THE BOUND MEANS, because it is load-bearing here and was not at first. An esm tolerance of `{abs: x}` ALONE is satisfied by a 1e-6 RELATIVE error -- the runner ORs the absolute bound with a default relative one -- so an absolute bound only binds when `rel: 0.0` is written beside it. Every assertion in this document pins `rel: 0.0`, and the indicators are `{abs: 0.0, rel: 0.0}`, which is genuinely exact rather than exact-looking. Verified by construction: with `rel` left implicit these assertions also pass at `abs: 0`, which is the tell. THIS COLUMN: case C step 1, a thin pack over soil that will later thaw, on SNOPAC's SUB-FREEZING branch, so the melt rate is exactly zero and the only surface water is what the routing decides. etp = -23.55 W/m^2, so the surface is gaining frost at 9.4e-09 m/s -- and under a pack that frost belongs to the SNOW, not the soil. This is the column where `dew_to_soil` = 0 is load-bearing: routing the frost into the soil as the snow-free default would moves the liquid tendency by about 6 % and turns three assertions red. The frozen sink is held at `sh2o` in the lower three layers and runs in the top one.
